verses.1: Is wisdom not calling out? Does understanding not raise its voice?
verses.2: At the highest points, above the crossroads, it stands firm;
verses.3: by the gates, at the city's doorways, it calls to the people.
verses.4: To you, people, I call out; my voice is directed to the human race.
verses.5: Pay attention, you simple-minded ones, to learning; you fools, set your hearts to understanding.
verses.6: Listen, for I speak what is noble, and from the opening of my mouth, what is upright.
verses.7: For my mouth speaks truth, and the words of my lips detest wickedness.
verses.8: All the words of my mouth are just; there is nothing crooked or twisted in them.
verses.9: They are all clear to the one who understands, and straight to those who find knowledge.
verses.10: Take instruction, and not silver; gain knowledge, and not gold refined.
verses.11: For wisdom is better than jewels, and all that you may desire cannot be compared to her.
verses.12: I, wisdom, dwell with prudence, and knowledge I find delight in.
verses.13: The fear of the LORD is to hate evil: pride, arrogance, and the evil way, and the twisted mouth I hate.
verses.14: Counsel and sound judgment are mine; I have insight, I have strength.
verses.15: By me, kings reign, and rulers decree justice.
verses.16: By me, rulers rule; by me, the mighty govern the people justly.
verses.17: I love those who love me, and those who seek me find me.
verses.18: Riches and honor are with me—enduring wealth and righteousness.
verses.19: My fruit is better than gold, better than fine gold; my yield is better than silver refined.
verses.20: I walk in the way of righteousness, in the center of the paths of justice,
verses.21: to give an inheritance to those who love me and to fill their treasuries.
verses.22: The LORD created me at the beginning of his works, before his deeds of old.
verses.23: From eternity I was established, from the beginning, before the earth was formed,
verses.24: when there were no depths, and no springs of water had yet been made,
verses.25: before the mountains were settled in place, before the hills I was brought forth,
verses.26: before he made the earth or the fields, or the dust of the world,
verses.27: when he prepared the heavens, I was there, when he drew a circle on the face of the deep.
verses.28: When he established the clouds above, and when he secured the fountains of the deep,
verses.29: when he set a limit for the sea, so that the waters should not transgress his command, and when he laid the foundations of the earth,
verses.30: I was by him, a trusted one, and daily I was his delight, rejoicing before him always,
verses.31: rejoicing in the inhabited world, and delighting in the human race.
verses.32: Now then, you children, listen to me; keep my ways well.
verses.33: Pay attention to instruction and gain understanding; do not turn away.
verses.34: Happy is the one who listens to me, watching at my doors daily, keeping watch at the posts of my entrances.
verses.35: For whoever finds me finds life and obtains favor from the LORD.
verses.36: But whoever acts wickedly harms their own soul; all who hate me love death.

notes:
Notes
- v. 22: The phrase "YHWH created me" (יְֽהוָה קָנָנִי) is rendered as "The LORD created me" to reflect the context of wisdom's origin as a divine creation.
- v. 23: The phrase "from eternity I was established" (מֵעוֹלָם נִסַּכְתִּי) uses "established" to convey the sense of being set in place from the beginning of time.
- v. 35: "Obtains favor" (יָפֶק רָצוֹן) is a rendering of the Hebrew idiom that suggests receiving favor or approval from the LORD.
- v. 36: "Acts wickedly" (חֹטְאִי חֹמֵס) is chosen to reflect the sense of willful transgression.
